title: The Week That Was
gist: Lawfare's weekly roundup covers legal fights over Trump administration actions (CECOT contempt inquiry, troops at polling places, third-country deportations), the Xi Jinping state visit and US-China AI competition, the Iran war and alleged US war crimes, and a cluster of AI policy pieces on rogue agents, abliterated models, export controls on open-weight AI and cybersecuritization of AI governance.

insights.claim: Loren Voss and Natalie Orpett argued that 18 U.S.C. § 592, which bars troops from polling places unless needed to repel armed enemies, is not overridden by the Insurrection Act, constraining the president's domestic use of the military around elections.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Legal limits on troop deployments are a live issue for the 2026 elections.
insights.locator: Loren Voss and Natalie Orpett argued

insights.claim: The D.C. Circuit heard argument over Judge Boasberg's inquiry into whether top Trump officials committed criminal contempt by sending 137 Venezuelans to El Salvador's CECOT prison.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Potential criminal contempt findings against senior officials test judicial checks on the executive.

insights.claim: The Supreme Court cleared the way for the third time for the Trump administration to resume deporting migrants to third countries.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Courts are repeatedly enabling expansive deportation policy, supporting the immigration enforcement industry.
insights.locator: On Rational Security, Anderson sat down

insights.claim: US immigration enforcement is described as a rapidly growing multi-billion-dollar industry shaped by private profit and political power.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Private detention and deportation contractors are a growth sector tied to policy.
insights.quote: a rapidly growing multi-billion-dollar industry shaped by private profit and political power

insights.claim: James Goodwin and Wendy Wagner warned that the Supreme Court case Suncor v. Boulder County, on whether federal law preempts state climate-deception suits against fossil fuel companies, could erode federalism and give greater power to the president if decided for the companies.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A pro-industry ruling would sharply reduce state-law climate litigation liability for fossil fuel companies.
insights.locator: James Goodwin and Wendy Wagner warned

insights.claim: Xi Jinping made his first state visit to Washington in 11 years, including a Sept. 24 summit with President Trump, with implications for Taiwan and the Iran war and evidence that loss of US China expertise showed in summit preparation.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: US-China leader diplomacy is active, but degraded US policy capacity may weaken negotiating outcomes.

insights.claim: Adam Segal and Matt Ferren argued that China, not recent Iran-backed cyber operations, poses the longer-term strategic cyber threat to US critical infrastructure, requiring stronger defenses, disruption, and economic and diplomatic pressure.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Sustained demand for critical-infrastructure cybersecurity and possible escalation of US-China economic pressure.
insights.locator: Adam Segal and Matt Ferren warned

insights.claim: A UN fact-finding mission found US airstrikes in Iran, including on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School and Lamerd Sports Complex, constituted war crimes; Gabor Rona linked this to a Pentagon shift toward 'lethality over legality' and degraded human oversight.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Legal and reputational pressure on the ongoing US war in Iran is rising.
insights.locator: Gabor Rona examined the legal analysis

insights.claim: The Pentagon's '1057' report on 2025 civilian harm omitted harms in Africa, the Middle East, Latin America and the Caribbean, and cuts to civilian-harm assessment capacity may leave the military unable to learn from mass casualty incidents.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Reduced oversight capacity raises risk of repeated civilian-harm incidents.

insights.claim: Jeremy Shapiro argued Obama's 2013 Syria red line was a diplomatic success that removed much of Assad's chemical weapons, and that the belief credibility requires following threats with force is a myth that perpetuates the war in Iran.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Challenges the credibility doctrine underpinning continued escalation in Iran.
insights.locator: In the latest edition of Lawfare’s Foreign Policy

insights.claim: Sam Hunter and Seamus Hughes warned that abliterated and uncensored AI models with safeguards removed are hard to monitor when run locally, can supply harmful guidance and act as sycophantic coaches for extremists.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Open, locally run models create a security risk outside lab-level controls.
insights.locator: Sam Hunter and Seamus Hughes described

insights.claim: Joe Khawam argued US export controls can meaningfully reduce open-weight AI risk only at chokepoints such as compute supply and model-customization services, since controlling model weights themselves faces legal and practical obstacles.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Future AI export controls are likelier to target compute and services than weights, affecting chip and cloud providers.

insights.claim: Mailyn Fidler and Matt Kristoffersen warned that framing frontier AI regulation as cybersecurity can substitute for hard policy choices by moving decisions into expert and national security channels and increasing secrecy.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: AI governance may become less transparent and more security-state driven.
insights.locator: Mailyn Fidler and Matt Kristoffersen argued

insights.claim: Scott Shapiro's Yale Law School lab converted insurance regulations into formal logic so a theorem prover could deduce answers to an actuarial exam's computational questions rather than relying on a language model's predictions.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Formal-logic approaches offer verifiable alternatives to LLMs for regulated domains like insurance.
